dedupe_keys.name: data centre energy use critical review of models and results iea 4e edna march 2025

description: This report reviews how data centre energy use has been estimated and why the estimates differ so widely. It identified and reviewed over 100 articles, reports and statistics published since 2014, covering thousands of estimates and projections for 2010 to 2040 across more than 200 scenarios and cases, and collated published energy data from 60 of the largest data centre operators since 2018. Estimates for 2020 range from under 200 TWh to 1,200 TWh and projections for 2030 from just over 200 TWh to nearly 8,000 TWh, a factor of almost 40; studies rated low quality, all using temporal extrapolation, gave 480 to 2,000 TWh for 2023. The authors propose five modelling approaches (bottom-up, aggregated totals, temporal proxy extrapolation, hybrid, other), rate each publication's methods on a six-point quality scale, identify the most plausible current range and set out best practices. Producer: commissioned by EDNA of the IEA 4E Technology Collaboration Programme and written by Kamiya (independent) and Coroamă (Roegen Centre for Sustainability), dated March 2025. Coverage: global, regional and country estimates. Access: a free PDF of 72 pages. Licence and cost: free; reuse terms were not in the pages read. Caveats: it is a literature review, not a new dataset, and the catalogued estimates are in the report's tables. Simulation uses: it guides the choice of assumptions and quality checks for data centre demand projections. Related record: the IEA Energy and AI dataset (data-iea-energy-and-ai).
